items.title: Ruth Lion interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: Kenny Dorham, and of course he was one of the great trumpeters of Blue Note.

ctx.x: Let’s talk about Art Blakey for a minute.

Oh yeah, Art Blakey. Well Blakey was, in my opinion, maybe the most exemplary of the Blue Note artists, because he did express what Alfred was looking for, which was that rhythm. And they had a great relationship — Blakey was just like his brother. And the Jazz Messengers, I have something I’d like to show you of that later, but that was one of the most successful of the records of the 50s, when they did Birdland, “One Night at Birdland,” and then they followed -- that was so successful with Blakey and Horace…
It’s almost like it could have been the Art Blakey jazz school too.
